newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan stocks close 0.33 pct higher.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan stocks close 0.33 pct higher.

text.p: Casablanca stock exchange closed on Thursday 0.33 percent as blue chips advanced slightly with cement firm Cior accounting for the main trade on the official market, stockbrokers said.
The bourse all-share index closed at 650.49 points from 648.38 points on Wednesday.

"Most stocks rose except for three which dipped very slightly. Volume traded on the official market was more substantial than what we have been used to in the past two months," a broker at ABN-AMRO Finance said.
Total traded volume on the official market was 47.7 million dirhams from 26.4 million dirhams.
Cior rose seven dirhams to 685 dirhams with 17,710 shares exchanged.
ONA group, the biggest Moroccan private conglomerate, and SNI, Societe Nationale d'Investissement, the second largest private group were up three dirhams each, to 815 and 750 dirhams respectively.
Credit firm Eqdom Credit rose five dirhams to 1,120 dirhams while mortgage firm Credit Hotelier et Immobilier advanced seven dirhams to 319 dirhams.
In banking, Wafabank and Banque Commerciale du Maroc gained seven dirhams respectively to reach 837 and 897 dirhams.
Second tranche of privatisation bonds, issued in May 1996, jumped 11 dirhams to 1,241 dirhams.
In the energy sector, Samir dipped 0.40 dirhams to 339.10 dirhams. Mining firm Societe Metallurgique d'Imiter gained nine dirhams to 570 dirhams.
On the over-the-counter market, the volume was 30.8 million dirhams from 106 million dirhams.
